spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates both spec forms — alpha(from … / N%) replacement and calc(alpha * k) scaling with the alpha keyword's number semantics — and probes support with CSS.supports on those exact declarations.

interactive.rationale: Color picker, two sliders, and mode toggles rebuild the declaration, painted swatch, and getComputedStyle read-back live; the fallback branch was observed active with the checkerboard swatch, 'fallback — not alpha()' tag, and a real color(srgb …/0.4) computed value.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises replace-vs-scale, a checkerboard swatch, the exact declaration, and real computed read-back — all delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: Origin-with-own-alpha, replace vs scale, and a two-tier honest fallback (rgb(from …) then plain sRGB, both labelled) cover the failure modes, with the unsupported banner citing the listing/detail/at-risk status discrepancy.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus 5070160203481088 (verified) and the css-color-5 relative-alpha spec anchor are linked.

conformance.rationale: The suite asserts the real contract (parse forms, computed replacement, calc scaling, none handling, display-p3 space preservation); its 8/8 failure in this Chromium 141 session is environment-expected since alpha() has not shipped here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI: fallback branch verified live via screenshot, DOM, and computed read-back with clean console (fonts.googleapis.com failure environmental); the native alpha() branch is unreachable in this browser and controls were not driven.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts distinguish native-paint success from labelled-fallback state, plus injected global error capture.

design_system.rationale: Pixel-verified defect: in the pressed mode button the inner / N% inherits color:var(--bg-ivory) while the global code rule keeps background:var(--bg-stone), rendering near-invisible ivory-on-stone (~1.02:1) — the rule-6 class of bug applied to nested code chips.

accessibility.rationale: Mode buttons use aria-pressed, the declaration line is aria-live, controls are labelled native inputs, and all swatch state is mirrored as text read-backs.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Harness-validated ok/ok recorded in responsive-support.json (2026-07-24) and the flex-wrapped controls fit narrow viewports; this session's own 360px CLI capture is inconclusive due to the headless min-width clamp.

openQuestions.title: Fix the invisible code chip inside the pressed mode button
openQuestions.detail: `.mode-btn[aria-pressed="true"]` overrides the button to black/ivory, but the nested <code> keeps the global bg-stone background while inheriting ivory text — the '/ N%' and '/ calc(alpha * k)' chips become ivory-on-stone (~1.02:1, pixel-sampled). Add e.g. `.mode-btn[aria-pressed="true"] code { background: transparent; color: inherit; border-color: currentColor; }` — same family as critical invariant 6.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the native branch once alpha() ships in stable
openQuestions.detail: The v152 listing says enabled-by-default while the detail says Proposed and the draft marks the feature at-risk; this session's Chromium 141 can only exercise the fallback. When a build with alpha() is available, verify the native swatch, computed serialization, and the conformance suite going 8/8.

summary: An honest, well-instrumented CSS lab: exact-surface support probing, real computed read-backs, and a clearly-labelled two-tier fallback that was observed working. One real visual defect: the code chips inside the pressed mode toggle are invisible (ivory text on the global stone code background, pixel-verified), the nested-element variant of the button-override trap. Verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshots, DOM, computed values, clean console); native alpha() is unavailable in this browser so only the fallback branch could be exercised, and controls were not driven.
